deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. The text is a German prose note on Greek history, continuing the account from the previous page (Epaminondas, Mantinea, Athens' renewed naval power). It covers Athenian moral decline and lack of patriotism, and good leaders pushed aside, especially by Chares. It then describes the Social War (the marginal heading reads 'Bundesgenossen Krieg'), which grew out of Athens' rising power. Cos, Rhodes and Chios form an alliance in '358' to defend their independence. Athens sends a fleet under Chabrias, which has to withdraw from the siege of Chios, and Chabrias is killed there. Timotheus and Iphicrates are sent against Byzantium but also fail. Athens is forced to make a peace granting its allies their freedom. The next page continues with the Sacred War ('2 Jahr darauf', dated 356). There is no derivation to reconstruct. The handwriting and content look like a history lesson notebook or school exercise filed in this bundle, not a Gauss mathematical working. Nothing implicit has been supplied.
errors: Historical dating: the Social War is usually dated 357–355 BC. The page gives 358 for the alliance; some sources put the start in 358/7, so this is a minor imprecision.

Simplification: Chares commanded together with Timotheus and Iphicrates in the Hellespont campaign. The operation against Byzantium was largely a diversion, and it ended with the failure at Embata (356) and recriminations against Timotheus and Iphicrates. The page compresses this.
The page names Cos, Rhodes and Chios but omits Byzantium as a member of the rebel coalition, though it is mentioned as a target.
Internal consistency: the next page dates the Sacred War to 356 as '2 Jahr darauf' after 358. This is consistent with the notebook's own dating; the usual date is 356/355 BC.
